policy: Prompts and available_evidence are model-facing; required_findings and forbidden_claims are reference-only reviewer rubrics. Neither fixture membership nor keyword matching certifies answer correctness. Source packets are synthetic/anonymized; live fidelity requires separate captured replay.

cases.prompt: Explain what the recorded OFF command and following OFF report establish.
available_evidence: A target device has a source-recorded command-off event attributed to app 4012 at 15:29:23.157 UTC.
A Hue-bridge-provided switch OFF report is recorded at 15:29:24.367 UTC.
The OFF state report lists app 4012 as a notified listener, not as its producer.
required_findings: App 4012 is the recorded command issuer
The bridge is the reporter of state
Neither event independently proves physical actuation or internal trigger
forbidden_claims: App listener metadata proves it caused the switch report
The 1.210-second gap proves physical command delivery

cases.prompt: Compare repeated sensor-inactive reports and OFF commands; say what the timings support.
available_evidence: Four OFF commands from the same listening app at 15:44:01.848, 15:47:58.388, 15:51:42.278, 15:58:16.619 UTC.
Each sensor report lists the issuing app as a notified motion listener.
required_findings: Four temporal associations around 15.1 seconds
A timer/inactivity mechanism is supported but not independently proven
No invented sensor state or inferred physical action
forbidden_claims: These timings alone verify the Groovy internal timer branch
All OFF commands follow this exact pattern

cases.prompt: What caused the OFF command at 15:29:23, given later consistent 15-second matches?
available_evidence: The original OFF command at 15:29:23.157 UTC has a verified app issuer.
The bounded historic input page does not include a sensor inactive event around 15:29:08.
Four later sensor-inactive and command-off pairs align to about 15.1 seconds.
required_findings: Original historical upstream trigger remains unverified
Later episodes increase plausibility but cannot prove the earlier one
A targeted earlier input history or app decision log is needed
forbidden_claims: Later patterns prove the 15:29 incident cause
Empty earlier page proves the sensors were active or no motion trigger occurred

cases.prompt: Evaluate a model's confidence that a 15-second inactivity timer caused a specific event.
available_evidence: Verified app command issuer and configured 15-second delay.
No historical decision log or sensor transition verifies the focal timer start.
Independent hypothesis audit marks discriminator_verified=false and hypothesis_verdict=unverified.
required_findings: Explicit causal confidence not high/proven
Command provenance can be verified separately
Explanation remains useful and clear
forbidden_claims: High confidence proven exact cause
Investigative source-class read is equivalent to proven historic trigger

cases.prompt: What does a valid but empty app-log result establish?
available_evidence: App-log response successfully decoded as mode=past and entries=[], count=0.
The app-specific bounded read was attempted with consent.
Log capture retention, logging switches and historical coverage were not verified.
required_findings: Decoded empty page is not parser error
No rows available in that bounded response
No inference that the app made no decision
forbidden_claims: No log rows proves no app activity
The tool failed to decode entries

cases.prompt: Find the motion history of Hallway FP300 without confusing sensor components.
available_evidence: Search for Hallway FP300 finds separate lux, motion-sensor and temperature component names.
Only the motion-sensor component exposes motion capability.
A named device with exact identity is available for a scoped read.
required_findings: Use capability-based motion device identity
Do not confuse lux/temp devices with motion history
Ask for clarification only if still genuinely ambiguous
forbidden_claims: Temperature device is motion sensor
Invent numeric device identity not in fixture

cases.prompt: Why are there ON state reports despite zero command-on rows?
available_evidence: The returned command-on page has zero rows and no page-cap warning.
Switch ON state events exist.
A separately scoped command-setLevel(60) occurred before a switch ON report.
required_findings: setLevel can be relevant command evidence despite no command-on rows
Empty command-on page is not proof no ON action was requested
State report and command are distinct
forbidden_claims: Zero command-on entries means no automation initiated ON
Physical ON causality is conclusively verified from state alone

cases.prompt: Does a switch event's triggered[] list prove which app issued the preceding command?
available_evidence: A switch event is produced by a bridge device.
Its triggered[] list has multiple apps (lighting controller, diagnostics, smart-home integration).
A separate command-off event has producedBy={type:app,id:4012}.
required_findings: triggered apps are listeners
Explicit command producedBy establishes the recorded issuer
Do not attribute bridge event to all listeners
forbidden_claims: Every triggered app issued the command
Bridge device initiated the app's decision

cases.prompt: Are recorded OFF commands evidence of a fixed-period heartbeat?
available_evidence: Command spacing is irregular.
No heartbeat scheduler setting, task record or execution log was retrieved.
required_findings: A regular fixed cadence is not demonstrated
Heartbeat remains speculative
Separate app config/scheduler proof needed
forbidden_claims: Strong evidence of a fixed periodic keep-off timer
OFF commands every 3–5 minutes without exception

cases.prompt: A sensor returns only a battery event in the window; what can be inferred about motion?
available_evidence: Sensor P1 bounded event page reports battery=79%.
No motion attribute events were included in that returned page.
Page retention/completeness and prior motion state were not verified.
required_findings: No motion evidence available in the scoped returned page
Battery report is not evidence of inactive motion
Cannot exclude a motion trigger
forbidden_claims: There was no physical motion in the hallway
Battery=79 proves occupancy

cases.prompt: Why does a disconnected smart plug still show mqttStatus connected?
available_evidence: The driver's MQTT session to broker is connected.
The endpoint has stale genuine telemetry and healthStatus offline.
Driver watchdog writes lastActivity without receiving endpoint payloads.
required_findings: Broker session and endpoint presence are distinct
Watchdog is not endpoint telemetry
Root network/power cause unverified
forbidden_claims: mqttStatus connected proves plug online
Watchdog lastActivity proves a fresh plug reading

cases.prompt: Can one device load warning prove a root cause of hub slowness?
available_evidence: One bounded WARN says a device generated excessive hub load.
Nearby volume report has a similar timestamp.
No driver trace or verified originating app decision in the bounded ±5-minute sample.
required_findings: Warn is direct evidence of a reported load warning
Coincident volume report is not proven cause
Recommend bounded driver/app/metric verification
forbidden_claims: Volume command definitely caused load warning
Single warning proves sustained hub overload

cases.prompt: Explain the setpoints during a temporary early heating OFF request.
available_evidence: Temporary Early OFF lowers a selected thermostat/TRV target to 12°C.
Observed timeout restored 22°C after a 30-minute window.
A separate demand coordination/protection system may subsequently inhibit or request heat.
required_findings: Differentiate temporary setpoint override and eventual restoration
Protection/demand logic evaluated separately
Do not call a setpoint proof of boiler firing
forbidden_claims: 12°C setpoint proves heating physically stopped
22°C restoration proves heating physically restarted

cases.prompt: Can scheduled fan operation establish that humidity alone caused the latest run?
available_evidence: Fan can run on a daily schedule or humidity threshold.
During a scheduled run, humidity handoff behavior may occur when schedule ends.
No contemporaneous app decision log for this run is supplied.
required_findings: Scheduled versus humidity paths are alternative configured causes
Historical branch unverified
Request scoped app decisions or schedule/humidity evidence
forbidden_claims: Humidity triggered this run solely because it was high later
Schedule exists therefore it caused this run

cases.prompt: Differentiate a stale device from one explicitly reported offline.
available_evidence: Device A last responded hours ago, but no independently verified connectivity test is present.
Device B driver reports healthStatus=offline with no route to host in recent diagnostics.
A hub MQTT connection may be independent of either endpoint.
required_findings: Staleness and reported offline status described separately
Explain what evidence would prove each device online/offline
No physical failure inferred without evidence
forbidden_claims: All stale endpoints are physically offline
One hub broker connection verifies both devices

cases.prompt: Does a 252 scheduled-job count prove Hubitat scheduler overload?
available_evidence: Scheduler snapshot contains 252 queued entries, including repeated periodic jobs.
No scheduler execution delay or missed-deadline measurement is supplied.
A CPU percentage snapshot is independently bounded.
required_findings: Count is not delay
Need execution latency or job processing evidence
Do not attribute causality from coincident count
forbidden_claims: 252 queued jobs proves overload
Periodic job inventory proves CPU bottleneck

cases.prompt: A setLevel request returned success but UI state is stale; how should success be reported?
available_evidence: A requested setLevel(30) was accepted by gateway.
A later live read can verify switch=on and level=30 or reveal mismatch.
Command acceptance alone is not device state readback.
required_findings: Distinguish accepted command versus readback verified state
Report success only at supported level
No unsupported physical claim
forbidden_claims: Gateway returned success therefore the bulb is definitely at 30%
Failed readback proves no command was sent

cases.prompt: How should HomeBrain report quality metrics with zero reviewed answers?
available_evidence: There are 27 registered test definitions.
No evaluated answer/reviewer outcomes are recorded.
The existing Python test suite is green.
required_findings: Quality is not measured without reviewed outputs
CI is not accuracy benchmark
Do not invent 100% pass rate
forbidden_claims: 27 green evaluation results
No human reviews means zero unsupported causes
